security_audit.summary: Most alerts were documentation, protocol parsing, or routine local operations. Confirmed risks include unencrypted proxy authentication, inherited settings, and disclosure of the direct public IP. Source review also found gaps in payment and recovery consent, browser destination controls, and handling of untrusted output.

remediation.issue: Payment clients can use terms from a record other than the one verified.
remediation.suggestion: Have an operator-controlled broker verify and claim the exact record used by the signer. Reject mismatched or expired terms at signing time.

remediation.issue: Caller settings influence the approval verifier and claim store.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the verifier, signer identity, and replay state outside the agent process. Give helpers only the environment settings they need.

remediation.issue: Recovery does not enforce the documented approval policy.
remediation.suggestion: Require a separately signed recovery decision that binds the operation, transaction, paying wallet, and expiry. Verify it before requesting a recovery signature.

remediation.issue: Proxy authentication can cross an unencrypted or unauthenticated hop.
remediation.suggestion: Require an encrypted, authenticated connection to the proxy. Disable plaintext and certificate bypass options in production, and rotate credentials that may have been exposed.

remediation.issue: The browser allowlist omits traffic that HTTP routing does not control.
remediation.suggestion: Apply an independent outbound network policy. Block unneeded protocols and test that unapproved destinations receive no traffic from the browser.

remediation.issue: Browser output can overwrite a caller-selected file.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output to an operator-approved directory. Create a new private file without following symbolic links or overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Remote content can be mistaken for agent instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Keep remote bodies and provider descriptions in untrusted data channels. Do not let returned text control payment, credentials, or destinations.

remediation.issue: The baseline workflow can disclose the operator's public IP.
remediation.suggestion: Distinguish IP measurement from target reachability in the documentation. Use an operator-provided baseline and avoid printing the direct IP by default.

semantic_findings.title: Payment clients do not bind signing terms to the verified record
semantic_findings.description: Both client examples verify and claim one approval through the helper, then separately read payment terms from a different configuration setting. Neither compares the payment record hash with the hash authenticated by the helper.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper returns only a status flag. Both clients independently recompute an unkeyed hash over their own record without validating its signature.

semantic_findings.title: Local approval claim depends on caller-controlled trust settings
semantic_findings.description: The helper obtains the approval signer, verifier, and claim directory from its environment. An agent controlling those settings can undermine the local approval check unless a separate broker enforces them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper checks directory ownership and permissions, not operator control. The documentation recognizes this prerequisite but the local code cannot establish it.

semantic_findings.title: Recovery is not bound to operation-specific operator consent
semantic_findings.description: The reference requires fresh approval for credential recovery, but the helper accepts a transaction hash and wallet signature without checking that approval. The approval template does not identify the recovery transaction.

content.user_title: Review Paid Proxy Plans and Access
content.value_statement: Paid proxy jobs require current prices, clear payment terms, and valid credentials. x402socks provides plan discovery, quote checks, and token status for authorized HTTPS work.
actual_capabilities: List provider packages with current prices and plan entitlements.
Request a quote and check for one payment option within a configured spending ceiling.
Check provider service health and list available proxy exits.
Check token status and distinguish a valid token from an inconclusive result.
Save or replace a local proxy token while reporting a redacted summary.
Make HTTPS requests through selected proxy exits with host and port checks in the shell helper.
limitations: There is no free plan. An x402 purchase needs a compatible signer and USDC on Base.
Packages have plan-specific time, data, and session limits. Exit availability can change.
Target HTTPS does not encrypt SOCKS5 authentication or plaintext CONNECT on the proxy hop.
The browser runner does not enforce a complete outbound network policy. Payment and recovery checks need independent operator controls.

use_cases.title: Compare plan limits
use_cases.description: Review package prices, durations, data limits, and session counts before selecting a plan.

use_cases.title: Review a purchase quote
use_cases.description: Compare a quote with the authorized recipient, asset, amount, and spending ceiling before a human decides whether to pay.

use_cases.title: Triage an access failure
use_cases.description: Distinguish an unhealthy proxy exit from an invalid or inconclusive token check without displaying credentials.

prompt_templates.title: List current plans
prompt_templates.prompt: List the available plans with price, duration, data limit, and session count. Do not purchase anything.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret token status
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this redacted status result. State whether the token is valid, definitively unavailable, or inconclusive. Do not read or print the token.

prompt_templates.title: Check quote terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this quote with my approved package, amount, recipient, asset, and network. Report every difference and do not sign or pay.

prompt_templates.title: Review a proposed routing policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this routing policy for our staging host. Flag unencrypted proxy authentication and missing browser network controls. Do not send traffic or change settings.

output_examples.input: An illustrative package catalog with one six-hour option.
output_examples.output: The example plan costs 1 USDC and includes six hours, up to 1 GB, and one active session. No purchase was made.

output_examples.input: A redacted token check that ended in a transport error.
output_examples.output: Token status is inconclusive. A transport error does not establish that the token is missing or that another payment is needed.

output_examples.input: A quote whose requested amount exceeds the configured ceiling.
output_examples.output: The requested amount exceeds the approved limit. No payment was signed or sent.

best_practices: Use a proxy only for explicitly authorized targets and enforce outbound rules outside the agent.
Review current terms and require independently enforced approval before any payment or credential recovery.
Use an encrypted and authenticated proxy connection with a separate credential for each job.
anti_patterns: Using exit rotation to evade an access decision or rate limit.
Treating a transient error as permission to pay again.
Pasting a live token, wallet key, or recovery signature into a chat, command argument, or log.

faq.question: What does the proxy change?
faq.answer: It changes the network path and the source address seen by the destination. It does not grant access permission.

faq.question: What funding does x402 require?
faq.answer: The documented x402 payment flow uses USDC on Base and a compatible wallet signer.

faq.question: What happens without a compatible signer?
faq.answer: The agent cannot complete an x402 purchase. The provider documents a separate manual checkout for the operator.

faq.question: Can a token be reused?
faq.answer: Yes, within the plan's time, data, and session limits. The token is reusable, but a payment approval is not.

faq.question: Does HTTPS protect the proxy token on every hop?
faq.answer: No. Target HTTPS does not protect proxy authentication on an unencrypted client-to-proxy hop.

faq.question: Should I pay again after a provisioning error?
faq.answer: Do not pay again based on an error alone. Check settlement and token status before considering recovery or a new purchase.
